scientific_hypothesis: A 29-layer alternating HfO2/MgF2 stack initialized at quarter-wave optical thicknesses for 267 nm center wavelength, with thickness optimization bounded to ±2.0 nm per layer, will produce higher target scores than the previous highly-scaled parameter inheritance approach, because the QWOT initialization places the design in a physically meaningful region of the solution space where UV transmission and visible/NIR rejection are simultaneously achievable through first-order interference.
expected_advantages: QWOT initialization places the design in a physically meaningful starting point
±2.0 nm bounds prevent divergence into unrealistic thickness regimes seen in iteration 18
29 layers provides sufficient degrees of freedom for bandpass shaping without exceeding manufacturing constraints
HfO2/MgF2 pair is a well-known UV-compatible material combination from recalled thin-film practice
known_risks: Uncertain: Exact refractive index values of HfO2 and MgF2 at 255-280 nm - the material catalog datasets will provide measured values but I am recalling approximate values of n_HfO2≈2.0-2.1 and n_MgF2≈1.38-1.40
Uncertain: Whether 29 layers is optimal versus a different layer count with cavity-defect topology - this route tests fixed 29-layer alternating topology only
Uncertain: Absorption coefficients (k values) in the UV for these materials - high k would reduce transmission regardless of interference design
Uncertain: Stress matching between HfO2 and MgF2 for space qualification - not modeled in TMM but relevant for actual deployment
Uncertain: Whether ±2.0 nm bounds are too restrictive to escape local minima - the feedback directive specifies this temporarily for 5 rounds
Risk: If best_target_score remains below 0.30 for three consecutive rounds, the perturbation bounds may need enlargement per the feedback directive
expected_observations: best_target_score should rise from iteration 15-18 values if QWOT initialization with tight bounds is more effective than inherited highly-scaled parameters
valid_candidates count should remain high (≥7) because ±2.0 nm bounds keep thicknesses in physically reasonable ranges
tightest_margin should not fall across rounds if the QWOT basin is stable
thicknesses_nm should cluster near 32.6 nm for hfo2 and 48.0 nm for mgf2 with ±2.0 nm variation
if best_target_score remains below 0.30 for three consecutive rounds, this indicates the perturbation bounds may be too restrictive
stop_conditions: if best_target_score improves by less than 1e-3 against the historical best for two consecutive rounds, treat the axis as exhausted, stop and keep the current best
if best_target_score remains below 0.30 for three consecutive rounds, relax the ±2.0 nm perturbation bound to ±5.0 nm and continue
if valid_candidates count falls below 5 for two consecutive rounds, the bounds may be too restrictive and should be enlarged
